title.en: Ora et labora: a life of prayer and work
title.ml: Ora et labora: പ്രാർത്ഥനയുടെയും അധ്വാനത്തിന്റെയും ജീവിതം

body.en: The Vallombrosan Benedictine Congregation belongs to the worldwide Benedictine Confederation and follows the Rule of St. Benedict. In India its monks live in the Oriental tradition of the Syro-Malabar Church.

The Vallombrosan Benedictine Congregation is a member of the worldwide Benedictine Confederation and follows the Rule of St. Benedict, the father of Western monasticism. Its guiding motto is Ora et labora, prayer and work.

The congregation was founded by St. John Gualbert in 1036 at Vallombrosa, near Florence. After his brother was murdered, John set out to take revenge. On Good Friday he came upon the murderer and was about to kill him, but the man begged for mercy in the name of Christ crucified. John forgave him, and that forgiveness awoke in him a deep love for the crucified Christ. He went to pray in the church of San Miniato in Florence, where, the tradition says, the crucifix bowed its head to him.

From an act of forgiveness came a life given entirely to God.

After years of prayer and reflection he founded the Vallombrosan congregation, giving first place to community life rooted in charity. By the time of his death there were nearly twelve monasteries across Italy.

By the founder’s will, the congregation exists for the vinculum caritatis et consuetudinis, the bond of charity and common life between its communities, which under the authority of the Abbot General help one another to safeguard and foster the consecrated life of their monks.

image_caption.en: The abbey church at Vallombrosa, near Florence

body.en:
In 1988, at the request of the then Abbot General, Dom Antonio Lorenzo Russo OSB, the Priory of Our Lady of Montenero in Livorno founded a seminary in the Diocese of Kottayam, Kerala, with the approval of Mar Kuriakose Kunnassery, Bishop of Kottayam. The community was founded in the Oriental tradition of the Syro-Malabar Major Archiepiscopal Church, with the authorisation of the Congregation for the Oriental Churches in Rome.

Formation began at the Carlos Dayara minor seminary at S.H. Mount, Kottayam, at first under priests of the Kottayam diocese appointed by Mar Kuriakose Kunnassery. The Priory of Montenero guided the formation of the candidates and the early growth of the Indian foundation. The first candidates completed their formation in India and then went to Italy, where they made their monastic profession.

Mar Mathew Moolakkattu, a diocesan priest of Kottayam, joined the congregation, completed his novitiate and made his monastic profession. Shortly after his solemn profession, on 6 January 1996, Pope Saint John Paul II appointed him Auxiliary Bishop of Kottayam. Today he is the Metropolitan Archbishop of Kottayam.

The hope of a traditional Benedictine monastery was there from the first years of the Indian community. Mar Kuriakose Kunnassery, then Metropolitan Archbishop, chose a beautiful hill at Kaduthuruthy for it and named the place Mariamala. After many years of waiting, the monastery was blessed on 29 June 2012.

In June 2016 St. Mary’s Monastery, Mariamala, was made an independent priory (sui juris priory). It is the headquarters of the Vallombrosan Benedictine Congregation in India, a meeting of Western monasticism and Eastern spirituality, and a spiritual centre for the Archeparchy of Kottayam and the Syro-Malabar Church.

Its monastic chapel holds the monastic choir, a distinctive part of the Benedictine tradition, built in harmony with the architecture of the Syro-Malabar Church.

The Vallombrosan Benedictines are a contemplative order whose monks centre their lives on prayer. Each monk is sustained by the daily celebration of the Eucharist and the Divine Office, and the meditative praying of the Office is the heart of a monk’s life.

Monks live this life of prayer in a community that fosters the joy of brotherhood, and each monastery is a living witness to the self-giving love of Jesus Christ. The quiet of a Benedictine monastery opens into meditation and prayer.

The monks also take part in manual work, education and pastoral service. Bringing prayer and work together is at the heart of Vallombrosan spirituality.

body.ml: സന്യാസ-പൗരോഹിത്യ ജീവിതത്തിലേക്ക് വിളി അനുഭവിക്കുന്ന യുവാക്കളെ കാർലോസ് ദയറയിൽ സ്വാഗതം ചെയ്യുകയും ഓരോ ഘട്ടത്തിലും അനുധാവനം ചെയ്യുകയും ചെയ്യുന്നു.

body.en: In Europe, Benedictine monasteries were centres of learning and culture. Continuing that tradition, the Vallombrosan Benedictines in Kerala run schools and an institute.

Benedictine monasteries are places of spiritual comfort and contemplation. The priest-monks of Mariamala are always ready to meet the spiritual needs of the faithful around them.

They serve in the Archdiocese of Kottayam and in other dioceses in India and abroad. The congregation’s monasteries include sanctuaries and basilicas where the monks hear confessions and lead devotions, and some monks serve in parishes.

Founded in 1999 and inaugurated on 18 June 2000 for the philosophical and theological training of candidates. Fr. Michael Kannala OSB, the first Indian monk to be professed, started the “Vallombrosa” Italian cheese factory here, whose cheeses are served in well-known restaurants across India, a living example of Benedictine manual labour. The house also offers residence to priests studying in Bengaluru and to students of Don Bosco College, T.C. Palaya.

T.C. Palaya P.O., K.R. Puram, Bengaluru 560036

Land at Nagamangalam near Hosur, Tamil Nadu, was acquired in 2002 for farming, and a monastic community followed. In the following year a spring was discovered whose water is believed to bring healing through the intercession of Our Lady, and a church was built in honour of Our Lady of Lourdes. Many pilgrims come to pray here. The monks welcome pilgrims, celebrate Holy Mass and care for the farm, poultry and buffaloes.

Nagamangalam P.O., Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu 635113

The first home of the Vallombrosans in India, where candidates are welcomed and begin their formation. It is named after Mar Charles Lavigne, first Vicar Apostolic of Kottayam. Its chapel of St. Benedict draws many faithful for Mass and the novena to St. Benedict.

This website brings together the story of the Vallombrosan Benedictines in Kerala, the monastic timetable, upcoming feasts, and news from Mariamala Monastery.

Content is being added in both English and Malayalam.
body.ml:
കേരളത്തിലെ വല്ലോംബ്രോസൻ ബെനഡിക്ടൈൻസിന്റെ ചരിത്രം, സന്യാസ സമയക്രമം, വരാനിരിക്കുന്ന തിരുനാളുകൾ, മരിയമല ആശ്രമത്തിൽ നിന്നുള്ള വാർത്തകൾ എന്നിവ ഈ വെബ്സൈറ്റിൽ ലഭ്യമാണ്.

ഉള്ളടക്കം ഇംഗ്ലീഷിലും മലയാളത്തിലും ചേർത്തുകൊണ്ടിരിക്കുന്നു.

body.en: St. Mary’s Monastery, Mariamala, was blessed on 29 June 2012 and became an independent priory in June 2016. It is the headquarters of the Vallombrosan Benedictine Congregation in India.
body.ml: കോട്ടയം ജില്ലയിലെ കടുത്തുരുത്തിക്കടുത്തുള്ള പഴുതുരുത്തിലാണ് മരിയമല ആശ്രമം (സെന്റ് മേരീസ് മൗണ്ട്). അർത്ഥികൾക്കായുള്ള മൈനർ സെമിനാരി കോട്ടയം എസ്.എച്ച്. മൗണ്ടിലും തത്ത്വശാസ്ത്ര-ദൈവശാസ്ത്ര പഠനഭവനം ബെംഗളൂരുവിലുമാണ്.
